d: The path a change takes, and where it can stop.

steps.b: Ordinarily a presbytery adopts the request and sends it to the Assembly. Presbytery has power to propose measures of common advantage to the church at large.

The stated clerk refers overtures seeking amendment of the book or the Assembly’s rules to the Committee on Constitutional Business for advice, and overtures proposing amendment of the Constitution to the Overtures Committee. The referral is final unless the Assembly redirects it.
A majority of those present and voting approves the proposed amendment to the Book of Church Order and recommends it to the presbyteries. For the Confession or Catechisms, three-fourths is required.

Two-thirds of presbyteries must give advice and consent for the Book of Church Order; three-fourths for the doctrinal standards. Presbyteries may not divide the parts of an amendment except as the Assembly directs.
A subsequent Assembly approves and enacts, by majority for the book and by three-fourths for the standards. Where too few presbyteries have reported, the Assembly may defer for a year.

d: Every gate between a man’s first application and his installation.

steps.b: He applies to the presbytery with jurisdiction over his church, with his Session’s endorsement, after at least six months membership. He is examined on experiential religion and motives, answers two questions and is enrolled as a candidate.

Examined in Christian experience and inward call, basic knowledge of doctrine, Bible content and church government, with a sermon on an assigned passage; states any differences with the standards; answers four questions; licensed for four years.

At least one year under presbytery’s supervision, in the full scope of ministerial duties. He may not administer the Sacraments. At the end it is approved or disapproved. Equivalent experience may be approved by a three-fourths vote.

A written call to definite work, ordinarily from a church, presbytery or the Assembly, with financial arrangements and assurance of liberty to preach the whole counsel of God, placed in his hands by presbytery.

Diplomas or their equivalent; examination in experiential religion and character, original languages, Bible content, theology, the Sacraments, church history, the history of this church, and government and discipline; a thesis; an exegesis; a sermon. Omissions require three-fourths with reasons recorded.
Sermon, recital of the proceedings, the ordination questions, the congregation’s questions, prayer with the laying on of the hands of presbytery, the right hand of fellowship, declaration and charge.

t: Electing a ruling elder or deacon
d: From the Session’s call for names to the laying on of hands.

steps.b: At times the Session determines, communicant members submit names, keeping the qualifications of 1 Timothy 3 and Titus 1 in view.

Nominees are instructed in the qualifications and work of the office, then examined in Christian experience and character, Bible content, the system of doctrine, government and discipline, the duties of the office, and willingness to assent to the ordination questions.
The Session reports those found eligible and gives at least thirty days notice of the congregational meeting. It may judge a man ineligible on Christian experience at any point in the process.

Communing members in good and regular standing vote; a majority of votes cast, excluding blanks and abstentions, elects. If a large minority is averse, the moderator seeks to dissuade the majority, but the election stands if the majority insists.

A sermon, a statement of the office, the questions to the candidate, the congregation’s question, prayer with the laying on of the hands of the Session, the right hand of fellowship, declaration and exhortation.

d: What a vacant church does, in order.

steps.b: The Session calls a congregational meeting to elect a pulpit committee, drawn from the congregation at large or the Session as the congregation designates.
After consultation and deliberation the committee recommends a candidate who meets the constitutional requirements of the office and is best suited to the congregation’s spiritual interests.
Ordered by the Session at the regular place of worship, with public notice of time, place and purpose at least one week before. A minister or ruling elder of this church presides if practicable.
Communing members in good and regular standing vote; a majority of votes cast, excluding blanks and abstentions, elects. A large minority is addressed under 20-5 before the call is pressed.
The moderator draws the call in due form, certifies the number not concurring and any facts of importance, and commissioners present and prosecute the call before presbytery.

Presbytery may recommend that the congregation desist, place the call in the man’s hands with or without advice, or decline to place it. A minister coming from another presbytery must be examined and received, and released by his own presbytery.

d: How a personal wrong becomes a judicial case, and where it should stop.

steps.b: The individual’s responsibility to admonish. Instruction in the Word comes first, and the steps must be followed in proper order.
If admonition is rejected, the calling of one or more witnesses.
If rejection persists, the church acts through her court. An injured party may not prosecute a personal offense without having tried these means first.
The court demands satisfactory explanations concerning reports affecting Christian character. If a strong presumption of guilt appears, it institutes process and appoints a prosecutor.

The charge is reduced to writing. At the first meeting the court appoints a prosecutor, orders the indictment drawn and served with the names of known witnesses, and cites the accused to appear not sooner than ten days later.
At the second meeting the charges are read and the accused pleads. If he takes issue, the trial is set not sooner than fourteen days after citation and follows the six-step order of 32-15.

The vote is taken, the verdict announced and judgment entered. Admonition or definite suspension concludes the process where the offender satisfies the court as to repentance; indefinite suspension or excommunication follows impenitence.

d: The route for a member who believes a court acted wrongly.

steps.t: Check that complaint is the right remedy
steps.b: Any communing member in good standing subject to the court may complain against any action of it. No complaint is allowable in a judicial case after process has commenced, though one filed then is held until the case ends.

steps.t: File with the court complained against
steps.b: Written notice with supporting reasons, filed with that court’s clerk within sixty days following the meeting.
At its next stated meeting, or a called meeting before then, provided the complaint was filed at least ten days in advance.
Written notice filed with the clerks of both courts within thirty days of notification of the decision. The same route is open if the lower court fails to consider it.

Notice does not suspend the action unless a third of those present when it was taken so vote. The court complained against appoints representatives; the parties are complainant and respondent; the complainant opens and closes the argument.
The higher court may annul the whole or part of the action, or send the matter back with instructions for a new hearing.

d: The route for a party against whom judgment was rendered.

steps.b: Appeal is open to those who submitted to a regular trial, those censured in a case without process, those whose censure was raised under 36-8, and those divested without censure under 34-10.
Notice may be given before the court adjourns. Written notice with supporting reasons is filed with the clerks of both courts within thirty days of notification.
The clerk of the lower court files the Record of the Case within thirty days of receiving notice. Nothing outside the Record is considered without the consent of the parties.

The judgment is suspended, though the court of original jurisdiction may, for recorded reasons and by a two-thirds vote, keep the appellant from the Table or from official functions, never as censure.
After the Record is read, each side has not over thirty minutes, the appellant opening and closing. The court votes on each specification of error in turn.
Affirm in whole or part, reverse in whole or part, render the decision that should have been rendered, or remand for a new trial, always with a written opinion.

d: From a gathering under supervision to a constituted church.

steps.b: On its own initiative, at a Session’s initiative, or on the written petition of an independent gathering. Outside presbytery bounds, an Assembly committee may exercise these powers.
An evangelist, or a mother church Session, or a commission serving as a temporary Session, with records submitted to presbytery for annual review.
Under chapter 57 so far as it applies. Those received are communing or non-communing members of this church, and rolls are kept separately.

When qualified men appear, nomination and election follow chapter 24 so far as it applies, normally at least two weeks before the organization service, with the new officers taking office at its completion.
The members sign a petition to presbytery. On approval, presbytery appoints an organizing commission and sets the date and time of the service.
Officers are ordained and installed, a pastor may be ordained or installed, the members enter into covenant with uplifted hand, and the commission declares them constituted a church.

steps.t: First acts of the new Session
steps.b: Elect a stated clerk, form a budget, and where there is no pastor elect a moderator and act to secure the regular administration of Word and Sacraments.
